_comment: The languages Obsidian itself offers, as a snapshot with the version it came from.
This is the list in the app's own Appearance > Language dropdown, which is the
only list that matters: it is what localStorage's `language` key can ever hold,
so a translation for anything outside it can never be read. It is deliberately
NOT the list in obsidianmd/obsidian-translations, which carries languages the
app does not ship — reading that one is how `el` and `sa` came to be recorded
here as things Obsidian supports when it has no code for either.
To refresh after an Obsidian update, read the map out of the installed app:
That prints the code-to-endonym map verbatim. Update `languages` and
`obsidianVersion` from it, then run `npm run check:lang`, which reports what
changed and what that means for src/lang/locales.ts and translations.ts.
_aheadOfHost: Languages this plugin ships that Obsidian has no code for. They cannot be
selected from Obsidian's own setting, only from the plugin's Language dropdown,
and they start working everywhere on their own if the app ever gains them.
When that happens the check below says so and the code moves out of this list.
